method: Visually inspected publisher iPhone screenshots in the App Store and screenshots in official product help pages. App Store promotional framing was distinguished from the app interface. No third-party artwork, prompts, or branding was copied.
limitations: Publisher screenshots demonstrate selected screens, not every state or the quality of the full app.
Visual judgments are design interpretations, not empirical proof of usability or authorship.
The sizing and color values below are TwoSpace implementation decisions, not measurements of other apps.

sources.observed: Question views prioritize a large prompt and an answer action; the purple promotional frames are separate from the app screens.
sources.application: Give the question chooser a distinct surface and readable prompt, then separate past responses below.

sources.observed: Home and memory screens give photographs most of the space, with small date labels and compact navigation.
sources.application: Let personal content take precedence over a decorative page banner.

sources.observed: Names, paired avatars, and response blocks distinguish people and their contributions.
sources.application: Make the author and response readable before showing secondary actions; preserve clear locked-answer states.

sources.observed: The shared character and room carry most of the visual personality, with a quieter surrounding interface.
sources.application: Keep expressive illustrations within activity content rather than scattering decoration across controls.

sources.observed: A dark Today screen prioritizes one main item and places secondary information below it. The official redesign rationale also describes this focus.
sources.application: Use clear priority and a limited set of dark surfaces; TwoSpace does not adopt the source app's gradients or health scoring.

sources.observed: Dark neutral surfaces allow artwork, titles, and primary playback actions to carry the hierarchy; rows often need no enclosing border.
sources.application: Keep base surfaces neutral, reserve rose for interactive emphasis, and avoid unnecessary nested cards.

sources.observed: The library grid and focused viewer serve different tasks. The official guide describes contextual controls and navigation adapted to each screen size.
sources.application: Separate browsing from editing and keep the drawing itself prominent. Do not imitate translucent native controls in the web app.

direction.typography: One system sans-serif, clear weight differences, readable body text, and no serif display titles or decorative uppercase labels.
direction.layout: Compact navigation; a distinct question focus; compact parallel activity choices; larger game boards; contextual drawing tools.
direction.inclusion: Remote shared experiences are meaningful without eventual in-person meetings. No relationship genders or reunion goals are assumed.

activityImplementation: Four compact tabs with a filled selected state; the first label is Ideas.
Two-column idea browsing on larger screens and one column on phones.
System-font question prompts with a subtle rose-tinted surface and separate answer blocks.
Dark game boards with two contrasting piece colors, initials, and a separate winning outline.
White drawing canvas and thumbnails preserve the appearance of existing stroke colors; controls remain dark.
Drawing swatches and tools use at least 44-pixel targets. Phone select controls retain 16-pixel text.

visualReview.environment: Fictional sample space in a separate Edge tab; desktop and 391 CSS-pixel phone layout. No personal entries were edited.
visualReview.finding: Browser inspection exposed a drawing-thumbnail sizing conflict: the shared button svg rule forced previews to 18 pixels high.
visualReview.fix: Explicit height:auto and an 8:5 aspect ratio restore the drawing thumbnail proportions. Phone drawing tools use four equal columns.
visualReview.attribution: Found and fixed by the assistant during visual review, not by the user.
